According to city officials and local authorities briefed on the event, the shooting took place in the 7000 block of West Anderson Lane, near U.S. 183, Research Boulevard, and Anderson Square. Austin-Travis County EMS transported the victim to a local hospital; a City of Austin notice stated that the man was alert and talking during transport. As of Sunday evening, officials had not released his name, age, or immigration status. The Austin Police Department (APD) confirmed that local officers were not involved in the encounter. APD units responded primarily to close a section of the southbound Research Boulevard frontage road at Anderson Square to manage traffic and secure the perimeter. Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) troopers also responded to the scene, noting that ICE is handling the core investigation. A dark-blue Toyota Corolla remained parked under the overpass following the incident, displaying visible damage to the passenger-side door and apparent bullet holes. A heavy law enforcement presence gathered behind police caution tape as onlookers assembled nearby. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and ICE have not answered preliminary questions regarding the operation, including why agents approached the vehicle, whether the man was an intended target, whether any officers sustained injuries, or if body cameras were active. ICE has yet to issue a formal public statement regarding the shooting.

PLD 2026 Supreme Court 393 Can a compromise or undertaking recorded before a Court be enforced through execution? The Supreme Court says yes. The dispute arose from inheritance Mutation No. 2534 dated 18.07.1996. The respondents challenged the mutation through a declaratory suit, claiming ownership on the basis of a gift deed dated 28.11.1994. During the proceedings, they undertook before the Peshawar High Court that if their suit failed, they would compensate the petitioners according to their share of the produce recorded in the mutation. The suit was eventually dismissed and the dismissal attained finality. The petitioners then sought execution of the undertaking. The matter later reached the Supreme Court, where the parties entered into a compromise on 01.06.2016. It was agreed that Mutation No. 2534 would be modified by reducing the share of the petitioners’ predecessor to 100 kanals, treating this as the final settlement of the disputed mutation. The petitioners thereafter filed a fresh schedule of the amount recoverable through execution. The Peshawar High Court ultimately dismissed the execution petition on 18.07.2024. The Supreme Court set that judgment aside. The Court held that an order passed on the basis of a compromise remains binding and enforceable even where no formal decree is drawn. Section 36 CPC makes the provisions relating to execution of decrees applicable, so far as may be, to the execution of orders. The Court relied upon Mehar Zulfiqar Ali Babu v. Government of Punjab (1997 SCMR 117), Ranjit Singh Hazari v. Juman Meah (PLD 1961 Dacca 842), Hassan Masud Malik v. Dr. Muhammad Iqbal (1995 SCMR 766) and Bakhtawar v. Amin (1980 SCMR 89). An undertaking voluntarily given before a Court has its own sanctity. A party cannot give an undertaking, have it recorded by the Court and then resile from it later. The Supreme Court also observed that the objections raised by the respondents sought to reopen matters which had already attained finality. An Executing Court cannot go behind the order it is called upon to execute. The High Court was therefore held to have erred in dismissing the execution petition. Impugned judgment dated 18.07.2024 was set aside and the Executing Court was directed to proceed with the execution in accordance with law. The important point is simple: a compromise or undertaking recorded by a Court is not merely an arrangement between the parties. Once it forms part of a judicial order, it carries legal force and can be enforced through execution.
